newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: S.Africa's Mandela in first state visit to Zimbabwe.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mandela in first state visit to Zimbabwe.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela began a three-day state visit to Zimbabwe on Monday, the first to the southern African nation by a South African head of state.

South Africa's first black president was welcomed at Harare Airport by Zimbabwe President Robert Mugabe, with whom he is due to hold talks on trade, bilateral issues and regional questions later in the day.
Mandela, widely revered here for his prolonged battle against apartheid, is also due to address Zimbabwe's parliament on Monday, becoming the first foreign head of state to do so.

Soon after his arrival Mandela attended a ceremony where the Harare City Council -- which awarded him the freedom of the city in 1990 following his release from 27 years in prison -- renamed one of town's main streets Nelson Mandela Avenue in his honour.
The former Baker Avenue houses the South African High Commission. Mandela becomes only the fourth head of state in the last 17 years to have a street named after him by the Zimbabwean authorities.

Mandela said the honour was a sign of the "undying friendship" between the two neighbouring states. Scores of black South Africans went into exile in Zimbabwe during the anti- apartheid struggle led by Mandela's African National Congress.
